subject: Consolidated subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence request
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@orthodata.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orthodata.com, OrthoData Security <security@orthodata.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at OrthoData is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Our security & procurement teams flagged a couple of items they need to complete our risk review before we can move to a pilot: 

1) A single, machine-readable roster of all subprocessors that process customer data (CSV or spreadsheet). We need name, primary function, country of residency, and whether they have access to encryption keys.
2) The most recent SIG-lite or CAIQ snapshot you can share and any SOC 2 scope statement (or link).
3) A short note on key residency / KMS ownership for model-serving and telemetry.

Can you confirm an ETA? Ideally we'd have the materials in the next 48 hours to keep procurement on schedule.

Appreciate it — looping in procurement and security on my side.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Senior Security Program Manager
OrthoData Inc.

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@orthodata.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide all three items. Quick plan:

- I'll attach a consolidated CSV with our current subprocessor roster (includes function, residency, and KMS access flags).
- I'll attach a SIG/CAIQ snapshot and a brief SOC 2 scope summary.
- For KMS: we'll include a short provenance summary that explains which keys are customer-dedicated vs Redwood-managed and the residency for each logical key.

Two notes:
- Our subprocessor roster is the operational list as of this morning (it includes ephemeral infra partners used for short-burst build/deploy jobs). If you need filtered views (e.g., only production-facing processors), tell me the filter and we can generate it.
- If you need an attested letter (pdf) for procurement, we can produce one but will need a PO or NDA in place depending on the details.

Attaching the CSV and initial artifacts now for your review. If procurement wants a one-page summary for legal, Ben (CC'd) can draft it.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_20280411.csv (CSV: name,function,country,residency,kms_access,notes)
- redwood_sig_caIQ_snapshot_20280411.pdf (SIG-lite mapped to CAIQ fields)
- kms_provenance_summary.txt (plain-text summary of key ownership and residency)

From: OrthoData Security <security@orthodata.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa@orthodata.com>, procurement@orthodata.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments. A couple follow-ups from the security review: 

1) In the CSV, could you add a column indicating whether subprocessors are in-scope for our SOC 2 (i.e., do they process customer PII or telemetry tied to customers)? A simple yes/no is fine.
2) For the KMS summary, can you confirm whether any keys used for inference model encryption are stored in a customer-managed HSM or only Redwood-managed KMS? If customer-managed HSM is an option, please indicate (yes/no) and what the integration pattern would be.
3) We see a transient infra partner listed with residency in a third country; can you confirm if they receive persisted customer data or only ephemeral build artifacts?

If you can answer #1 and #2 in-line and update the CSV, we should be able to move to internal approvals. Last ask: do you have a canonical URL (or doc) that points to the SOC 2 scope and the auditor's name? That helps our compliance tracker.

Thanks,
OrthoData Security

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: OrthoData Security <security@orthodata.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa@orthodata.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi — quick answers inline and a note on next steps.

1) SOC 2 in-scope flag: Updated the attached CSV with an "in_scope_for_soc2" column; values = yes/no. The transient infra partner you flagged is marked as "no" — they only receive ephemeral build artifacts and do not persist customer data. We included a short note in the CSV notes column to explain the retention window.

2) KMS and HSM: By default Redwood manages encryption keys used for model-serving. We support customer-managed keys via KMS integration and, for customers with strict HSM requirements, can integrate with customer-provisioned HSMs in private deployments. Short summary: 
- Default: Redwood-managed KMS (keys in region indicated in CSV).
- Customer-managed KMS: supported (bring-your-own-key); keys can be stored in customer cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and we can be configured to use them for data-at-rest encryption.
- HSM option: supported for Private deployments — we can document integration steps and provide a technical contact to scope the work.

3) SOC 2 scope doc and auditor: Our SOC 2 Type II audit (last completed coverage period: 2027-07-01 to 2028-06-30) was conducted by Meridian Audit Partners. The SOC 2 scope includes: Production inference services, telemetry ingestion pipeline (non-identifiable telemetry), and the Redwood Console for observability. I'll place the auditor name and scope doc in the Drive folder and post the link in a follow-up.

Next steps: Jonas will create a filtered CSV (production-only) if you want that view for procurement; Ben can prepare an attestation letter if procurement needs one. If you confirm you'd like a filtered roster and an attestation, we'll produce both within one business day.

Link to SOC 2 scope & artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGH-JkLmnop

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

Attachments (updated):
